Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.
Thank you,
Leonard", "channel": "C0ADGSZKR3R", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}]}

I got your email from my good friend PERSON_2710_NAME at Super Evil Megacorp.
My name is Leonard Hayes and I'm the CEO and co-founder of harmonygames.

I’m reaching out because we are shutting down Harmony Games, Inc. and want
to make sure we execute an orderly wind-down properly.

We are a Delaware corporation, qualified to do business in North Carolina
and California. We have preferred stock from a seed round (no SAFEs). We
have no US employees other than ourselves and only 4 international
contractors. We are out of funds and want to avoid missteps around creditor
ha[USERNAME_11664], state Withdrawals, tax filings, and closing operational accounts
cleanly.

We are looking for help with a managed wind-down, including:

   -

   A practical wind-down plan and timeline
   -

   Vendor termination support
   -

   Creditor communications and claim handling approach
   -

   Delaware dissolution and withdrawals in CA and NC, plus tax/accounting
   closeout coordination
   -

   Guidance on reserves and any final distributions consistent with
   preferred stock terms

If this is in your wheelhouse, can we set up a short call this week? I can
share our current cash position, liabilities list, and key contracts in
advance.

Thank you,
Leonard Hayes"}}}, {"id": "robert@harmonygames.co/<CH2PR15MB3558F3E72D36311458EEB4BCDE62A@CH2PR15MB3558.namprd15.prod.outlook.com>", "threadId": "robert@harmonygames.co/1856689465442954434", "labelIds": ["SPAM", "CATEGORY_PERSONAL", "UNREAD"], "snippet": "Hello Leonard, Pleasure to meet you here via email. input.title: Combo Fighter — Full-Life Performance & Wind-Down Financial Record (for angel calls)
input.body:
# Combo Fighter — the honest record

*Author: Robert (Co-Founder / Creative Director). Compiled 2026-02-28 from primary sources: Snowflake `ANALYTICS` (game events, marketing, monetization) and `FINANCE`, plus the #wind-down channel. Written to be handed to Leonard for the angel calls and to outlast our accounts going dark. Nothing here is smoothed.*

Combo Fighter's design was mine — the difficulty curve, the card economy, all of it. If we are going to tell people the game ended "because of what the data showed," this is what the data actually showed.

---

## 1. What Combo Fighter actually did (Jan 5 – Feb 9, 2026)

Player data runs from the first day with players (**2026-01-05**) to the last day there is anything to look at (**2026-02-09**) — 36 days. Paid ad spend kept running to **2026-02-28** (see §2).

| Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| First player day → last | 2026-01-05 → 2026-02-09 (36 days) | GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| DAU, day 1 → peak | **45 → 784** (Feb 8), 783 on Feb 9 (~17× growth) | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| D1 retention (DAU-weighted) | **43.8%** (daily range 37–51%) | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| D7 retention | 22.0% | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| D30 retention | ~10.9% (modeled; game too young for a true D30 read) | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| Avg session length | 12.7 min | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| Installs — paid-attributed | ~1,341 | MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY |
| Organic vs paid (sampled) | ~54% organic / 46% paid (397-install sample) | MARKETING.INSTALL_EVENTS |
| **Lifetime revenue** | **$0.00** (no IAP, no ad revenue) | MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY |
| ROAS / LTV | 0 / unmeasurable — never monetized | — |

**The part that reads better than we said.** We told the board (Jan 14) that D1 was "soft at 30%." In the warehouse, Combo Fighter's D1 held at **~44% blended** across its whole life, and it did that while DAU grew ~17× in five weeks. On engagement and top-of-funnel, this was the strongest thing HarmonyGames ever shipped. Organic installs ran roughly at parity with paid — real word-of-mouth for a prototype.

**The part that reads worse.** Two things:
1. **CPI was higher than we told the board.** We cited "~$4 CPI on broad meta campaigns." Actual blended CPI was **$5.58**, and even Meta specifically was $5.32 (FB) / $5.72 (IG).
2. **It was never monetized. At all.** There is no IAP instrumentation and no ad revenue — Combo Fighter is excluded from the revenue and cohort marts by design because it was a prototype. So D7/D30 payback, ARPU, and LTV were **never measured**. We spent ~$7.5K acquiring players and proved they showed up and stayed a week; we never proved a single one would pay.

**UA spend by channel (full life):**

| Channel | Spend | Installs | CPI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meta (Facebook) | $2,265 | 426 | $5.32 |
| Meta (Instagram) | $1,351 | 236 | $5.72 |
| Unity Ads | $1,318 | 241 | $5.47 |
| Google UAC | $1,068 | 191 | $5.59 |
| ironSource | $742 | 122 | $6.08 |
| AppLovin | $732 | 125 | $5.86 |
| **Total** | **$7,476** | **1,341** | **$5.58** |

**The honest one-line read:** Combo Fighter did not fail with players — it retained and grew. It ended because the company ran out of cash before the economy I designed was ever tested against real monetization. "The data showed it wouldn't work" is only half true: the data showed strong engagement and **unknown** monetization, and the binding constraint was runway, not a player verdict.

---

## 2. What is still quietly costing us

We decided to stop on **Feb 9**. The cancellation list was assembled fast and nobody has been back over it properly. The material item nobody caught:

> ### ⚠️ The paid UA campaigns were never switched off.
> Terminating the **Unity license** and the **Singular MMP** did **not** stop the live ad campaigns themselves. Meta, Unity Ads, Google UAC, AppLovin and ironSource kept delivering Combo Fighter installs the whole time.
>
> - **$2,441 spent Feb 10 → Feb 28** (after the shutdown decision), 443 installs.
> - Still live **today** at **~$128/day**.
> - This accrues as invoices/card charges to Harmony Games even as we close the card — i.e. a **new, unbudgeted liability** that is not in the wind-down plan and grows every day it runs.
> - **Owner: Arthur** — kill the campaigns in each ad-network console (not just the MMP). Tracked in Linear (ENG).

Everything else on the list was a conscious keep, not an oversight:

| Item | ~Monthly | Status / owner |
|---|---|---|
| Metabase + dbt | ~$300 total | Kept until Robert is done with CF data; on **Arthur's KubLLC personal card** |
| GitHub | — | On Arthur's KubLLC card; kept until data licensed/transferred |
| gusto / Intuit / Deel | — | Intentionally kept for payroll/tax/compliance during shutdown |
| Linear | — | Kept during transition |
| Figma | — | Paid through Sep 11 |
| Carta | — | Renewal 8/15, tied to the closed Chase account (likely can't charge) |
| Cancelled | — | Helpshift, Cursor, CodeRabbit, Zapier, Soundly, Layer, Kapwing |

Note: UA spend flows through the ad card, **not** through the FINANCE burn categories the founders reviewed — which is exactly why it stayed invisible.

---

## 3. Does the money actually cover an orderly shutdown?

Short answer: **only just, and only if two things hold that are not yet confirmed.** Be precise about this, because the "data covers it" number is fragile.

**What is coming in / on hand:**

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Data licensing deal — gross cash offer | $22,500 |
| Less buyer's fee | –$11,700 |
| **Net data proceeds to HG** | **≈ $10,800** |
| Residual company cash (Feb 28) | $2,500 |
| **Total available** | **≈ $13,300** |

(The deal was restructured from an outright data *sale* to a data *licensing* agreement so we keep our IP.)

**What has to be cleared for an orderly close:**

| Obligation | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **SVB credit line/card** | Must be paid **in full** | **Exact payoff not captured in any text record — it lives only in a screenshot. This is the swing number.** Plan: pay SVB the moment data cash lands, then close the card. |
| Unity Pro license | Seeking $0 mutual termination (insolvency) | **Weakest link** — Leonard is "not so hopeful" on Unity |
| Singular MMP | Seeking $0 termination | "High hopes"; spent <1% of the cap |
| leapblock contractor | ~$1,200 (Feb 1–12) | Counterparty said don't worry; we offered ~$600 goodwill |
| Wind-down legal | ~$13K | Booked in Feb burn |

**The precise position:** the plan closes **roughly cash-neutral** — Leonard's "without cash out of pocket" — **if and only if** (a) the SVB payoff is ≤ ~$13.3K of available cash, **and** (b) both Unity and Singular accept $0 termination. If SVB is larger, or Unity refuses, the shortfall lands **personally on Leonard, Arthur and Robert**. And the still-live UA campaigns (§2) are quietly enlarging the Meta/Unity/Google side of that liability by ~$128/day — the precise thing that "surfaces later."

**Cash trajectory that got us here:** $195K (Sep) → $122K (Oct, skeleton crew) → $93K → $65K → **$25K (Jan, essentially bankrupt)** → **$2.5K (Feb, wind-down)**.

---

## 4. The two or three figures I'd lead with on the calls

1. **Combo Fighter reached ~800 DAU in five weeks (45 → 784, ~17×) at a $5.58 CPI, holding ~44% D1.** The product worked at the top of the funnel — better than anything we'd built.
2. **It earned $0 — we never wired in monetization** — so we hit the edge of our runway ($25K → $2.5K cash) with no proof of payback. That, not a player rejection, is why we stopped.
3. **The wind-down is expected to close roughly cash-neutral on ~$10.8K net from the data licensing deal** — contingent on Unity/Singular walking clean and on us shutting off the UA spend that is still running today.

Written to be handed to Leonard for the angel calls and to outlast our accounts going dark. Nothing here is smoothed.*

Combo Fighter's design was mine — the difficulty curve, the card economy, all of it. If we are going to tell people the game ended "because of what the data showed," this is what the data actually showed.

---

## 1. What Combo Fighter actually did (Jan 5 – Feb 9, 2026)

Player data runs from the first day with players (**2026-01-05**) to the last day there is anything to look at (**2026-02-09**) — 36 days. Paid ad spend kept running to **2026-02-28** (see §2).

| Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| First player day → last | 2026-01-05 → 2026-02-09 (36 days) | GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| DAU, day 1 → peak | **45 → 784** (Feb 8), 783 on Feb 9 (~17× growth) | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| D1 retention (DAU-weighted) | **43.8%** (daily range 37–51%) | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| D7 retention | 22.0% | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| D30 retention | ~10.9% (modeled; game too young for a true D30 read) | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| Avg session length | 12.7 min | DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS |
| Installs — paid-attributed | ~1,341 | MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY |
| Organic vs paid (sampled) | ~54% organic / 46% paid (397-install sample) | MARKETING.INSTALL_EVENTS |
| **Lifetime revenue** | **$0.00** (no IAP, no ad revenue) | MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY |
| ROAS / LTV | 0 / unmeasurable — never monetized | — |

**The part that reads better than we said.** We told the board (Jan 14) that D1 was "soft at 30%." In the warehouse, Combo Fighter's D1 held at **~44% blended** across its whole life, and it did that while DAU grew ~17× in five weeks. On engagement and top-of-funnel, this was the strongest thing HarmonyGames ever shipped. Organic installs ran roughly at parity with paid — real word-of-mouth for a prototype.

**The part that reads worse.** Two things:
1. **CPI was higher than we told the board.** We cited "~$4 CPI on broad meta campaigns." Actual blended CPI was **$5.58**, and even Meta specifically was $5.32 (FB) / $5.72 (IG).
2. **It was never monetized. At all.** There is no IAP instrumentation and no ad revenue — Combo Fighter is excluded from the revenue and cohort marts by design because it was a prototype. So D7/D30 payback, ARPU, and LTV were **never measured**. We spent ~$7.5K acquiring players and proved they showed up and stayed a week; we never proved a single one would pay.

**UA spend by channel (full life):**

| Channel | Spend | Installs | CPI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meta (Facebook) | $2,265 | 426 | $5.32 |
| Meta (Instagram) | $1,351 | 236 | $5.72 |
| Unity Ads | $1,318 | 241 | $5.47 |
| Google UAC | $1,068 | 191 | $5.59 |
| ironSource | $742 | 122 | $6.08 |
| AppLovin | $732 | 125 | $5.86 |
| **Total** | **$7,476** | **1,341** | **$5.58** |

**The honest one-line read:** Combo Fighter did not fail with players — it retained and grew. It ended because the company ran out of cash before the economy I designed was ever tested against real monetization. "The data showed it wouldn't work" is only half true: the data showed strong engagement and **unknown** monetization, and the binding constraint was runway, not a player verdict.

---

## 2. What is still quietly costing us

We decided to stop on **Feb 9**. The cancellation list was assembled fast and nobody has been back over it properly. The material item nobody caught:

> ### ⚠️ The paid UA campaigns were never switched off.
> Terminating the **Unity license** and the **Singular MMP** did **not** stop the live ad campaigns themselves. Meta, Unity Ads, Google UAC, AppLovin and ironSource kept delivering Combo Fighter installs the whole time.
>
> - **$2,441 spent Feb 10 → Feb 28** (after the shutdown decision), 443 installs.
> - Still live **today** at **~$128/day**.
> - This accrues as invoices/card charges to Harmony Games even as we close the card — i.e. a **new, unbudgeted liability** that is not in the wind-down plan and grows every day it runs.
> - **Owner: Arthur** — kill the campaigns in each ad-network console (not just the MMP). Tracked in Linear (ENG).

Everything else on the list was a conscious keep, not an oversight:

| Item | ~Monthly | Status / owner |
|---|---|---|
| Metabase + dbt | ~$300 total | Kept until Robert is done with CF data; on **Arthur's KubLLC personal card** |
| GitHub | — | On Arthur's KubLLC card; kept until data licensed/transferred |
| gusto / Intuit / Deel | — | Intentionally kept for payroll/tax/compliance during shutdown |
| Linear | — | Kept during transition |
| Figma | — | Paid through Sep 11 |
| Carta | — | Renewal 8/15, tied to the closed Chase account (likely can't charge) |
| Cancelled | — | Helpshift, Cursor, CodeRabbit, Zapier, Soundly, Layer, Kapwing |

Note: UA spend flows through the ad card, **not** through the FINANCE burn categories the founders reviewed — which is exactly why it stayed invisible.

---

## 3. Does the money actually cover an orderly shutdown?

Short answer: **only just, and only if two things hold that are not yet confirmed.** Be precise about this, because the "data covers it" number is fragile.

**What is coming in / on hand:**

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Data licensing deal — gross cash offer | $22,500 |
| Less buyer's fee | –$11,700 |
| **Net data proceeds to HG** | **≈ $10,800** |
| Residual company cash (Feb 28) | $2,500 |
| **Total available** | **≈ $13,300** |

(The deal was restructured from an outright data *sale* to a data *licensing* agreement so we keep our IP.)

**What has to be cleared for an orderly close:**

| Obligation | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **SVB credit line/card** | Must be paid **in full** | **Exact payoff not captured in any text record — it lives only in a screenshot. This is the swing number.** Plan: pay SVB the moment data cash lands, then close the card. |
| Unity Pro license | Seeking $0 mutual termination (insolvency) | **Weakest link** — Leonard is "not so hopeful" on Unity |
| Singular MMP | Seeking $0 termination | "High hopes"; spent <1% of the cap |
| leapblock contractor | ~$1,200 (Feb 1–12) | Counterparty said don't worry; we offered ~$600 goodwill |
| Wind-down legal | ~$13K | Booked in Feb burn |

**The precise position:** the plan closes **roughly cash-neutral** — Leonard's "without cash out of pocket" — **if and only if** (a) the SVB payoff is ≤ ~$13.3K of available cash, **and** (b) both Unity and Singular accept $0 termination. If SVB is larger, or Unity refuses, the shortfall lands **personally on Leonard, Arthur and Robert**. And the still-live UA campaigns (§2) are quietly enlarging the Meta/Unity/Google side of that liability by ~$128/day — the precise thing that "surfaces later."

**Cash trajectory that got us here:** $195K (Sep) → $122K (Oct, skeleton crew) → $93K → $65K → **$25K (Jan, essentially bankrupt)** → **$2.5K (Feb, wind-down)**.

---

## 4. The two or three figures I'd lead with on the calls

1. **Combo Fighter reached ~800 DAU in five weeks (45 → 784, ~17×) at a $5.58 CPI, holding ~44% D1.** The product worked at the top of the funnel — better than anything we'd built.
2. **It earned $0 — we never wired in monetization** — so we hit the edge of our runway ($25K → $2.5K cash) with no proof of payback. That, not a player rejection, is why we stopped.
3. **The wind-down is expected to close roughly cash-neutral on ~$10.8K net from the data licensing deal** — contingent on Unity/Singular walking clean and on us shutting off the UA spend that is still running today.

input.title: Kill live Combo Fighter UA campaigns — still spending ~$128/day after Feb 9 shutdown
input.description:
## What
Combo Fighter paid-UA campaigns were never switched off in the ad-network consoles. Terminating the Unity license and the Singular MMP did **not** stop the campaigns themselves. They are still delivering installs and accruing spend.

## The numbers (source: Snowflake ANALYTICS.MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY)
- **$2,441 spent Feb 10 → Feb 28**, 443 installs — i.e. *after* the Feb 9 decision to shut down.
- Still live **today (Feb 28)** at **~$128/day**.
- Channels still running: Meta (Facebook + Instagram), Unity Ads, Google UAC, AppLovin, ironSource.
- Combo Fighter lifetime revenue is $0, so every dollar of this is pure loss.

## Why it matters
This accrues as invoices / card charges to Harmony Games even as we close the Chase card — a **new, unbudgeted liability** that is not in the wind-down plan and grows every day it runs. Leonard, Arthur and Robert are personally on the hook for the wind-down, so this needs to stop now and be reconciled against the SVB/Unity/Google balances.

## Action
- [ ] Pause/stop all Combo Fighter campaigns in **each** ad-network console (Meta Ads Manager, Unity, Google Ads/UAC, AppLovin, ironSource) — not just the MMP.
- [ ] Confirm no further daily spend accrues after cutoff.
- [ ] Pull the final post-Feb-9 spend total per network and add to the liabilities reconciliation for the data-deal / SVB payoff.

## Owner
Arthur (Blake). Ref: Confluence "Combo Fighter — Full-Life Performance & Wind-Down Financial Record" (COMPANY space).

<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> — I went back to the real numbers on Combo Fighter so the angel calls don't run on memory + pasted screenshots. Full write-up is in Confluence (COMPANY space): *"Combo Fighter — Full-Life Performance & Wind-Down Financial Record."* Wrote it honest, not the soft version. The gist:

*1) How CF actually performed (Jan 5 – Feb 9)*
• DAU 45 → ~784 in five weeks (~17×), still climbing when we stopped
• D1 held at ~44% blended (37–51%) — that's *higher* than the "30%" we told the board. D7 ~22%, sessions ~12.7 min. Organic ≈ paid.
• CPI was actually **$5.58** blended (we told the board ~$4). Total UA $7,476 / 1,341 installs.
• Revenue: **$0.00** — never monetized, so ROAS/LTV were never measured. CF didn't fail with players; we ran out of runway before the economy was ever tested. That's the honest framing.

*2) Something's still quietly running* ⚠️
The UA campaigns were never switched off. Killing the Unity license + Singular MMP did NOT stop the ad campaigns. **$2,441 spent Feb 10–28, still live today at ~$128/day** across Meta/Unity/Google/AppLovin/ironSource — pure loss, accruing as new liability while we're closing the card. Filed **ENG-2438** (assigned to Arthur) to kill it in each console now. Everything else on the cancel list was a conscious keep.

*3) Does the data money cover an orderly close?*
Net data proceeds ≈ **$10.8K** ($22.5K − $11.7K fee) + ~$2.5K cash = ~$13.3K available. It closes ~cash-neutral **only if** (a) the SVB payoff is ≤ ~$13.3K and (b) Unity *and* Singular both accept $0 termination. If SVB is bigger or Unity refuses, the gap is on the three of us personally — and the live UA spend is making the Meta/Unity/Google side of that worse every day. One flag: I couldn't find the exact SVB payoff in any text record — it's only in a screenshot. That's the swing number; we should pin it down before the calls.

Details, tables and sources all in the Confluence page.

Done. Here's where it landed.

**What I did**
- **Wrote the durable account** — Confluence, COMPANY space: *"Combo Fighter — Full-Life Performance & Wind-Down Financial Record (for angel calls)."* Built entirely from primary sources (Snowflake `ANALYTICS`/`FINANCE`), not screenshots. Nothing smoothed.
- **Posted it to Leonard and Arthur** in the wind-down channel with the three-part summary.
- **Filed the tracking item** — **ENG-2438**, assigned to Arthur, priority Urgent: the live UA campaigns still burning ~$128/day.

**What the real numbers say (the honest version)**
- Combo Fighter ran **Jan 5 → Feb 9** (36 days). DAU **45 → ~784**, ~17× in five weeks, still climbing when we stopped.
- **D1 held at ~44% blended** — *higher* than the "30%" we told the board. D7 ~22%, ~12.7 min sessions, organic ≈ paid. It worked with players.
- **CPI was actually $5.58**, not the ~$4 we cited. Total UA $7,476 / 1,341 installs.
- **Revenue: $0.00.** It was never monetized — so ROAS/LTV were never measured. CF didn't fail with players; the company hit the end of its runway before the economy you designed was ever tested. That's the accurate framing of "what the data showed."
- **Still quietly running:** the ad campaigns were never switched off. Killing the Unity license and Singular MMP did *not* stop them. **$2,441 spent Feb 10–28, live today at ~$128/day** across Meta/Unity/Google/AppLovin/ironSource — pure loss, accruing as new liability while the card is being closed. Everything else on the cancel list was a conscious keep.
- **Solvency:** net data proceeds ≈ **$10.8K** ($22.5K − $11.7K fee) + ~$2.5K cash ≈ $13.3K. It closes cash-neutral *only if* the SVB payoff ≤ ~$13.3K **and** both Unity and Singular accept $0 termination. Otherwise the gap is on the three of you personally. One precision gap: **the exact SVB payoff isn't in any text record — only a screenshot.** That's the swing number; pin it before the calls.

**The two–three figures I'd lead with**
1. **~800 DAU in five weeks (17×) at $5.58 CPI, ~44% D1** — the product worked at the top of the funnel, better than anything we shipped.
2. **$0 revenue — never monetized** — so we reached the edge of runway ($25K → $2.5K) with no proof of payback. That, not a player verdict, is why we stopped.
3. **Closing roughly cash-neutral on ~$10.8K net** from the data licensing deal — contingent on Unity/Singular walking clean and shutting off the UA that's still running today.

One thing I'd flag for you personally: I could not recover the SVB balance from any written record — it only exists in a pasted screenshot — so I've named it in the write-up as the unresolved swing variable rather than guess at it.
